simple: Chat commands are special messages that start with a slash, like `/mute`, that make something happen. Roblox has some built-in ones, and you can make your own with `TextChatCommand`. This example makes `/super` double your character's size and `/mini` halve it. It is the safe, modern way to add commands to your game.
analogy: It is like a secret password at a clubhouse. When someone says the exact word, the door opens and something special happens.
keyPoints: Turn on Roblox's built-in commands by setting `TextChatService.CreateDefaultCommands` to true in the Properties window.
Add your own command by inserting a `TextChatCommand` inside `TextChatService`.
Set `PrimaryAlias` and `SecondaryAlias` to the words that trigger it, like `/super` and `/mini`.
Connect to the command's `Triggered` event in a Script in ServerScriptService. It gives you the `TextSource` (who typed it) and the message.
Use `string.split(message, " ")` to break the message into words and check the first one.
The example scales the character by changing the `NumberValue` children of the Humanoid, like body height and width.

terms.alias: Another name for the same thing. `/super` and `/mini` are two aliases for the same command object.
terms.PrimaryAlias: The main word that triggers the command, like `/super`.
terms.SecondaryAlias: A second word that triggers the same command, like `/mini`.
terms.Triggered: The event that fires when a player sends one of the command's aliases.
terms.TextSource: Represents the player who typed the command. Use its `UserId` to find the `Player`.
terms.string.split: Breaks text into pieces. `string.split("/super now", " ")` gives `{"/super", "now"}`.
terms.NumberValue: An object that holds one number. Humanoids have some that control body scale, so doubling them doubles the size.

example.title: Make /super and /mini commands
example.place: Script in ServerScriptService (with a TextChatCommand named SizeCommand inside TextChatService, PrimaryAlias `/super`, SecondaryAlias `/mini`)
example.code:
local TextChatService = game:GetService("TextChatService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local sizeCommand: TextChatCommand = TextChatService:WaitForChild("SizeCommand")

sizeCommand.Triggered:Connect(function(textSource, message)
	-- Work out how much to scale by
	local scaleMult = 1
	local words = string.split(message, " ")
	if words[1] == "/super" then
		scaleMult = 2
	elseif words[1] == "/mini" then
		scaleMult = 0.5
	end

	-- Find the player and their Humanoid
	local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(textSource.UserId)
	local character = player and player.Character
	local humanoid = character and character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid")
	if not humanoid then
		return
	end

	-- Multiply every scale value on the Humanoid
	for _, child in humanoid:GetChildren() do
		if child:IsA("NumberValue") then
			child.Value *= scaleMult
		end
	end
end)
explain: We wait for the `SizeCommand` object you added in Studio.
When a player types `/super` or `/mini`, `Triggered` runs with who typed it and what they typed.
We split the message into words and check the first word to pick 2 (bigger) or 0.5 (smaller).
We find the player's Humanoid, stopping early if anything is missing.
We multiply each scale `NumberValue` on the Humanoid. A height scale of 1 becomes 2 with `/super`.

watchOut: Spelling the alias without the slash. Set it to `/super`, not `super`.
Naming the command object something other than SizeCommand while the script waits for SizeCommand. The script will wait forever.
Spamming `/super` multiplies again each time: 1, then 2, then 4, then 8. Add a limit if you do not want giant players.
